questions.question: Who is the custodian of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** is recognized as the **custodian** and **final interpreter** of the Constitution. It possesses the ultimate authority to interpret constitutional provisions and ensure their sanctity is maintained.
 
• Under the power of **Judicial Review**, the court can examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders. If any law is found to be in violation of the **Constitution**, the Court has the power to declare it null and void under **Article 13**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** acts as the **Guardian of Fundamental Rights**. According to **Article 32**, citizens have the right to move the apex court directly for the enforcement of their rights through various writs such as **Habeas Corpus**, **Mandamus**, and **Quo-Warranto**.
 
• It preserves the **federal equilibrium** by resolving legal disputes between the **Union Government** and the **States**, or between two or more States, ensuring that each entity operates within its constitutional limits.
 
• Through the landmark **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**, the **Supreme Court** established the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, preventing the **Parliament** from amending the essential features that form the foundation of the **Indian Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• The **President of India** is the **nominal head** of the state. While the President takes an oath under **Article 60** to protect and defend the Constitution, they do not have the judicial authority to interpret it or strike down laws.
 
 
 
• **Parliament**:
 
 
• The **Parliament** is the supreme **legislative body**. Under **Article 368**, it has the power to amend the Constitution, but these amendments are subject to the **Supreme Court’s** oversight to ensure they do not violate the **basic structure**.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**:
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the **real executive head** and leads the **Council of Ministers**. The PM is responsible for governance and policy implementation but lacks the constitutional role of being a 'custodian' or 'guardian' of the legal document.

questions.question: The tenure of Chief Election Commissioner is:

options.text: 6 years or till 65 years of age
6 years or till 62 years of age

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 years or till 65 years of age**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the **Union** and **State** levels.
 
• Under the provisions of the **Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991**, the **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)** and other Election Commissioners hold office for a term of **six years**.
 
• There is an upper age limit of **65 years**; if the individual reaches this age before completing the six-year term, they must vacate the office.
 
• The **CEC** is appointed by the **President of India** and occupies a position of significant constitutional importance to ensure free and fair elections.
 
• The **Constitution of India**, specifically **Article 324**, provides the framework for the appointment and powers of the commission to maintain its **independence** from executive interference.
 
• The **CEC** can only be removed from office through a process of **impeachment** by **Parliament**, which is identical to the removal process of a **Judge of the Supreme Court**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure and Composition**:

 
 
• The **Election Commission** originally functioned as a single-member body but was converted into a **multi-member body** consisting of one **CEC** and two **Election Commissioners** since **October 1993**.
 
• All commissioners have equal **decision-making powers** and receive salaries and allowances equivalent to those of a **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
 
 
• **Mandate**:
 
 
• The commission manages elections for the **Lok Sabha**, **Rajya Sabha**, **State Legislative Assemblies**, **Legislative Councils**, and the offices of the **President** and **Vice President**.
 
• It does not handle **Panchayat** and **Municipality** elections, which are conducted by **State Election Commissions**.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of weight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton (N)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weight** is defined as the measure of the **gravitational force** acting on an object. Because weight is a type of force, it follows the same **International System of Units (SI)** as force.
 
• The mathematical relationship for weight is expressed by the formula W = m times g , where **m** represents the mass of the object and **g** represents the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• The standard value of **g** on Earth is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, meaning weight varies depending on the **gravitational field strength** of a location (e.g., weight on the Moon is roughly 1/6th of that on Earth).
 
• The **Newton (N)** is the derived unit of force in the SI system, named after the scientist **Sir Isaac Newton** to honor his contributions to **classical mechanics**.
 
• One **Newton** is defined as the amount of force required to accelerate a mass of **1 kilogram** at a rate of **1 meter per second squared** (1 N = 1 kg·m/s²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kilogram (kg)**:

 
 
• It is the **SI base unit** for **mass**, which measures the quantity of matter in an object.
 
• Unlike weight, **mass** is an **intrinsic property** and remains constant regardless of the object's location in the universe.
 
 
 
• **Joule (J)**:
 
 
• It is the **SI unit** for **energy**, **work**, and **heat**.
 
• One Joule is defined as the work done when a force of one **Newton** moves an object through a distance of one **meter** in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Pascal (Pa)**:
 
 
• It is the **SI unit** of **pressure** and **stress**.
 
• One Pascal is equivalent to one **Newton per square meter** (1 N/m²), used to quantify internal **mechanical stress** or **atmospheric pressure**.

questions.question: What was Ruskin Bond's debut novel, for which he won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957?

options.text: Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Room on the Roof**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Room on the Roof** is the celebrated debut novel written by the prolific Indian author **Ruskin Bond** when he was merely **17 years old**.
 
• The novel was first published in **1956** by Andre Deutsch and gained international recognition shortly after its release.
 
• In **1957**, Ruskin Bond was awarded the **John Llewellyn Rhys Prize**, a prestigious British literary award given to a writer from the Commonwealth under the age of 30, making him one of its youngest recipients.
 
• The semi-autobiographical story is set in the scenic town of **Dehra Dun** and follows the life of **Rusty**, an orphaned **Anglo-Indian** boy struggling to find his identity and belonging.
 
• The book is celebrated for its evocative descriptions of the **Himalayan foothills** and its sensitive exploration of **adolescent rebellion**, friendship, and the transition into adulthood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Blue Umbrella**:

 
 
• A popular novella published in **1980**, centered on a young girl named **Binya** in a small village in **Garhwal**.
 
• It was adapted into a **National Award-winning** film by director **Vishal Bhardwaj** in 2005.
 
 
 
• **A Flight of Pigeons**:
 
 
• A historical novella published in **1978**, set during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• The story depicts the experiences of an English family in **Shahjahanpur** and was adapted into the film **Junoon** by **Shyam Benegal**.
 
 
 
• **Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra**:
 
 
• This is a collection of semi-autobiographical short stories published in **1991**.
 
• For this work, Ruskin Bond was honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1992**, one of India's highest literary honors.

questions.question: The historic 1983 Cricket World Cup final, where India defeated the West Indies, was held at which iconic venue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord's, London**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The final of the **1983 ICC Cricket World Cup**, also known as the **Prudential Cup**, was held on **June 25, 1983**, at the historic **Lord's Cricket Ground** in **London**.
 
• **India**, under the captaincy of **Kapil Dev**, faced the **West Indies**, who were the dominant force in world cricket and the winners of the previous two editions in **1975** and **1979**.
 
• Batting first, the Indian team was bowled out for a modest total of **183 runs** in **54.4 overs** of the then-standard **60-over** format, with **Kris Srikkanth** top-scoring with **38 runs**.
 
• In a stunning defensive bowling display, India dismissed the legendary West Indies lineup for just **140 runs** in **52 overs**, securing a historic **43-run victory**.
 
• This victory marked India's **first-ever World Cup title** and is credited with fundamentally changing the landscape of cricket in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohinder Amarnath**:

 
 
• He was awarded the **Man of the Match** in the final for his crucial contribution of **26 runs** and a bowling spell of **3 wickets** for **12 runs**.
 
 
 
• **Lord's Cricket Ground**:
 
 
• Established in **1814** and named after its founder **Thomas Lord**, it is internationally recognized as the **Home of Cricket**.
 
• It houses the **MCC Museum**, the oldest sports museum in the world, containing the famous **Ashes Urn**.
 
 
 
• **Other Noted Venues**:
 
 
• **Old Trafford**: Based in **Manchester**, this venue hosted the first **semi-final** of the **1983 World Cup**, where India defeated **England**.
 
• **The Oval**: Located in **Kennington, South London**, it hosted the very first **Test match** in England in **1880**.
 
• **Headingley**: Situated in **Leeds**, it is the home of **Yorkshire County Cricket Club** and hosted several group matches during the **1983 tournament**.

questions.question: During the planning era, import substitution industrialization (ISI) in India aimed to

options.text: Encourage exports of manufactured goods for foreign exchange earnings
Attract foreign investment in consumer goods industries
Replace imports of manufactured products with domestic production through protectionist policies
Liberalize imports of machinery and capital goods without restrictions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Replace imports of manufactured products with domestic production through protectionist policies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI)** was a trade and economic policy adopted by **India** during the **Planning Era** to achieve the goal of **economic self-reliance**.
 
• The primary objective of this strategy was to replace **foreign imports** with **domestically produced goods**, thereby reducing the country's dependence on developed nations for essential industrial products.
 
• This strategy was deeply rooted in the **Mahalanobis Model**, which steered the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)** toward the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
• The government utilized **protectionist policies**, including **high import tariffs** and **quantitative restrictions (quotas)**, to shield infant **domestic industries** from the competitive pressure of foreign manufacturers.
 
• The logic behind **ISI** was to conserve **foreign exchange reserves** and stimulate **domestic manufacturing** growth by ensuring a captive market for local producers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Protectionist Mechanisms**:

 
 
• **Tariffs**: These are taxes imposed on **imported commodities**, making foreign goods more expensive and less attractive to local consumers.
 
• **Quotas**: These specify the **maximum quantity** of a good that can be imported, providing a physical barrier to entry for foreign products regardless of price.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Focus**:
 
 
• Unlike **Export-Oriented Industrialization (EOI)**, which focuses on producing for international markets, **ISI** is an **inward-looking trade strategy** focused on the domestic market.
 
• The policy aimed to create a diversified **industrial structure** ranging from consumer electronics to **capital goods** like steel and heavy machinery.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Policy**:
 
 
• While **ISI** helped build a massive industrial base, it eventually led to inefficiencies and a lack of innovation due to lack of competition, necessitating the **1991 Economic Reforms**.
 
• The **1991 reforms** shifted India from protectionism toward **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)**.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian batsman to score a triple century in Test cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virender Sehwag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Virender Sehwag** etched his name in history as the first Indian batsman to score a triple century in **Test cricket** on **March 29, 2004**.
 
• He achieved this monumental feat against **Pakistan** at the **Multan Cricket Stadium**, scoring **309 runs** off **375 balls**.
 
• This extraordinary performance earned him the iconic title of **'Multan ka Sultan'** and helped **India** secure its first-ever Test victory on Pakistani soil.
 
• His innings included **39 boundaries** and **6 sixes**, famously reaching the **300-run mark** with a six off the bowling of **Saqlain Mushtaq**.
 
• Before this, the record for the highest individual Test score by an Indian was held by **VVS Laxman**, who scored **281** against **Australia** at **Eden Gardens** in **2001**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virender Sehwag**:

 
 
• He is one of only four batsmen globally to have scored two triple centuries in **Test cricket**, joining the ranks of **Don Bradman**, **Brian Lara**, and **Chris Gayle**.
 
• His second triple century, a blistering **319 runs** against **South Africa** in **2008** at **M.A. Chidambaram Stadium**, remains the highest individual score by an Indian in Test matches.
 
 
 
• **Karun Nair**:
 
 
• He became the second Indian to score a triple century, hitting **303 not out** against **England** at **Chennai** in **December 2016**.
 
 
 
• **Sachin Tendulkar** and **Rahul Dravid**:
 
 
• Despite being the leading run-scorers for India, neither achieved a triple century. **Tendulkar's** highest Test score is **248 not out** against **Bangladesh** (**2004**), while **Dravid's** highest is **270** against **Pakistan** (**2004**).

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Credit Guarantee Fund for MSMEs & Startups?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Collateral-free guarantee support**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary objective of the **Credit Guarantee Fund** is to facilitate the flow of **institutional credit** to the **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME)** sector and recognized **Startups** by providing a guarantee cover for credit facilities.
 
• This fund allows borrowers to access loans without the requirement of **collateral security** or **third-party guarantees**, which are traditionally the biggest barriers for new entrepreneurs and small businesses in securing bank finance.
 
• The **Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)** was established by the **Ministry of MSME**, Government of India, and the **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** to implement the scheme.
 
• For startups, the **Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)** provides credit guarantee cover up to a specified limit, often reaching **Rs. 10 crore** per borrower, to encourage **innovation** and **entrepreneurship** across the country.
 
• Under these schemes, the trust settles a significant portion of the **outstanding amount** (ranging from **75% to 85%**) in the event of a default by the borrower, thereby reducing the **risk perception** of lending institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS):**

 
 
• It is operated by the **National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC)** under the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**.
 
• The scheme covers credit extended by **Scheduled Commercial Banks**, **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**, and **SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)**.
 
• Eligibility is restricted to startups that are recognized by the **DPIIT** and have reached a certain stage of **revenue generation** or **funding**.
 
• The **CGTMSE** scheme was formally launched in **August 2000** and has since undergone several enhancements to include a wider range of **Member Lending Institutions (MLIs)** and increased credit limits.

questions.question: Which of the following pair regarding respiration is correct? I. Anaerobic – presence of oxygen II. Aerobic – absence of oxygen
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I** suggests that **Anaerobic respiration** occurs in the presence of **oxygen**; however, by definition, anaerobic processes take place strictly in the **absence of oxygen**. In this metabolic pathway, **glucose** is only partially oxidized, leading to the formation of by-products such as **ethanol** or **lactic acid** rather than complete breakdown. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement II** characterizes **Aerobic respiration** as occurring in the absence of oxygen, but this process essentially requires **molecular oxygen** to function as the **terminal electron acceptor** in the **electron transport chain**. This pathway allows for the total oxidation of **glucose** into **carbon dioxide** and **water**, releasing a significantly higher amount of **cellular energy**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aerobic Respiration**:

 
 
• This process occurs in both the **cytoplasm** (glycolysis) and the **mitochondria** (Krebs cycle and ETC) of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It is highly efficient, producing an estimated net gain of **36 to 38 ATP** molecules per molecule of glucose.
 
• It is the primary mode of respiration for most higher organisms, including **humans**, **animals**, and **plants**.
 
 
 
• **Anaerobic Respiration**:
 
 
• This process occurs entirely within the **cytoplasm** and does not require mitochondrial involvement.
 
• It yields a much lower energy output, typically only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
• In **yeast**, this is known as **alcoholic fermentation**, while in **human muscle cells** during intense exercise, it results in **lactic acid fermentation**, which can cause muscle cramps and fatigue.
 
• Organisms that can only survive in environments lacking oxygen are known as **obligate anaerobes**.

questions.question: Swabhav Swachhata Sanskaar Swachhata campaign 2024 has been built around ____ key pillars.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2024** campaign, themed **Swabhav Swachhata Sanskaar Swachhata**, was organized from **17th September to 2nd October 2024** as a massive precursor to **Gandhi Jayanti**.
 
• The campaign is structured around **three key pillars** designed to accelerate the vision of a **Garbage-Free India** and celebrate the **10th anniversary** of the Swachh Bharat Mission.
 
• **Pillar 1: Swachhata Ki Bhaagidari (Public Participation, Awareness, and Advocacy)** focuses on large-scale **Jan Bhagidari** to mobilize citizens through **cleanliness pledges**, workshops, and community-led initiatives to foster sustainable behavioral change.
 
• **Pillar 2: Swachhata Lakshit Ekayi (Cleanliness Target Units - CTUs)** involves the identification and time-bound transformation of **black spots** or neglected areas that are difficult to clean, ensuring targeted intervention in high-traffic or high-waste zones.
 
• **Pillar 3: Safai Mitra Suraksha Shivirs** is dedicated to the welfare of **sanitation workers**, providing **preventive health screenings**, distribution of safety equipment, and facilitating access to **social security schemes** such as **PM-JAY** and **PM-SVANidhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)**:

 
 
• Launched on **2nd October 2014**, the mission aimed to eliminate **open defecation** and improve **solid waste management** across India.
 
• It consists of two sub-missions: **SBM-Urban**, managed by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**, and **SBM-Gramin**, managed by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
 
• The mission is currently in its **Phase II**, focusing on **ODF Plus** status and 100 percent processing of municipal solid waste.
 
• The **Swachhata Hi Seva** initiative is a recurring annual event that serves as a call to action for every citizen to contribute to cleanliness through **Shramdaan**.

questions.question: Who succeeded Chandragupta I as the ruler of Gupta empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Samudragupta** was the son and chosen successor of **Chandragupta I** and the Lichchhavi princess **Kumaradevi**, ascending the throne around **335 CE**.
 
• The **Prayag Prashasti** (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed in Sanskrit by his court poet **Harisena**, provides a detailed account of his succession, stating that **Chandragupta I** publicly declared him the most worthy heir.
 
• He is often referred to as the **'Napoleon of India'** by historian **V.A. Smith** due to his extensive military conquests across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During his reign, he adopted a policy of **Digvijaya**, defeating nine kings in **Aryavarta** (Northern India) and twelve kings in **Dakshinapatha** (Southern India).
 
• He performed the **Ashvamedha** (horse sacrifice) to proclaim his imperial sovereignty and issued diverse gold coinage, including types depicting him as a **musician** playing the **Veena**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta II**

 
 
• Also known as **Vikramaditya**, he was the son of **Samudragupta** and is famous for defeating the **Shaka** rulers of Western India.
 
• His court was adorned by the **Navaratnas** (nine gems), including the legendary poet **Kalidasa**.
 
 
 
• **Kumaragupta II**
 
 
• A later ruler of the **Gupta Dynasty** who reigned during the late 5th century (around **473–476 CE**) as the empire began to weaken.
 
 
 
• **Budhagupta**
 
 
• He was one of the last major emperors of the **Gupta Empire**, ruling from approximately **476 CE to 495 CE**, maintaining control over a large territory before the final decline caused by **Huna** invasions.

questions.question: ‘Deodhani’ dance is associated with which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deodhani** is a traditional folk dance from the Indian state of **Assam**, specifically prevalent in the **Lower Brahmaputra Valley**, including regions like **Kamrup**, **Darrang**, and **Mangaldoi**.
 
• The dance is deeply rooted in religious mythology and is performed to propitiate the snake goddess **Manasa** (also known as **Maroi**) during the **Manasa Puja** or **Maroi Puja** festival.
 
• It is considered a **shamanistic** dance where the performer, known as a **Deodhani** (female) or **Deodha** (male), is believed to enter a state of **trance** and become possessed by the deity.
 
• The performance is characterized by high-energy, semi-classical movements, featuring intense **head-shaking**, swirling of unbraided hair, and the mimicry of a **cobra's movements**.
 
• Accompanying music is provided by traditional instruments such as the **Khol** (a terracotta drum), **Tal** (cymbals), and the **Ciphung** (flute), which create a rhythmic environment conducive to the spiritual ritual.
 
• Historically, the dance often involves the use of ritualistic props like **swords** and **shields**, showcasing ancient martial influences combined with folk spirituality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam's** Diverse Dance Forms:

 
 
• **Bihu Dance**: A world-renowned folk dance performed during the **Rongali Bihu** to celebrate the harvest and the **Assamese New Year**.
 
• **Sattriya**: One of the eight **Classical Dances of India**, introduced by the 15th-century saint **Srimanta Sankardev** in the **Sattras** (monastic institutions).
 
• **Bagurumba**: A rhythmic folk dance of the **Bodo community**, often called the **Butterfly Dance** due to its light and graceful movements.
 
• **Bhortal Dance**: Developed by **Narhari Burha Bhakat**, it is known for the use of large cymbals and fast beats.
 
 
 
• Other States Mentioned:
 
 
• **Bihar**: Famous for folk dances like **Jat-Jatin**, **Bideshiya**, and the **Paika** dance, which is a martial art form.

questions.question: In the context of launch vehicle of India, the GSLV Mk-III can carry weight up to ____ kg into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbits.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **GSLV Mk-III**, recently renamed as **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3)**, is the heaviest and most powerful launch vehicle in the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** fleet.
 
• It is specifically designed to deliver heavy communication satellites, weighing up to **4,000 kg**, into the **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
• The vehicle utilizes a **three-stage** propulsion system, which includes two **S200 solid rocket boosters**, an **L110 liquid core stage**, and a high-thrust **C25 cryogenic upper stage**.
 
• The **C25 stage** is powered by the **CE-20**, India's largest indigenous cryogenic engine, which provides the necessary impulse to reach high-altitude orbits.
 
• By achieving a **4-tonne** lift capacity to **GTO**, India has gained the ability to launch its **INSAT** and **GSAT** series satellites without relying on expensive foreign commercial launch services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Capacity**:

 
 
• While its **GTO** capacity is **4,000 kg**, the **LVM3** can carry much heavier payloads, approximately **8,000 kg** to **10,000 kg**, into **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
 
 
• **Major Mission Successes**:
 
 
• The **GSLV Mk-III** was the launch vehicle for the **Chandrayaan-2** mission in **July 2019** and the successful **Chandrayaan-3** mission in **July 2023**.
 
• It has been designated as the carrier for the **Gaganyaan** mission, which is **India's first manned spaceflight** program.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions and Fuel**:
 
 
• The vehicle stands **43.5 meters** tall and has a lift-off mass of **640 tonnes**.
 
• The **S200 boosters** are among the largest solid propellant boosters in the world, containing **205 tonnes** of propellant each.

questions.question: In India, between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5, the use of clean cooking fuel has increase from 44% to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**59%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)**, conducted between **2019 and 2021**, provides a comprehensive overview of household amenities and health indicators in **India**.
 
• According to the survey, the proportion of households using **clean cooking fuel** increased from **43.8%** in **NFHS-4 (2015-16)** to **58.6%** in **NFHS-5**, which is rounded to **59%**.
 
• **Clean cooking fuel** as defined by the survey includes **Electricity**, **LPG/Natural Gas**, and **Biogas**.
 
• The increase of nearly **15 percentage points** over five years highlights the significant progress made in providing safe energy sources to Indian households.
 
• The data reflects the narrowing gap in energy access, although a considerable difference still exists between the **urban** and **rural** demographics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Detailed NFHS-5 Insights**:

 
 
• **Urban-Rural Disparity**: While **89.7%** of urban households used clean cooking fuel in **NFHS-5**, only **43.2%** of rural households had access, despite rural areas showing higher growth rates compared to previous years.
 
• **Government Schemes**: The **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)**, launched in **May 2016**, has been a major driver in increasing **LPG** penetration among **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** families.
 
• **Health and Environment**: Transitioning to clean fuel is crucial for achieving **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7** and reducing **Indoor Air Pollution**, which causes serious **respiratory diseases** among women and children.
 
• **Solid Fuel Usage**: Despite the rise in clean fuel, many rural households still rely on **wood**, **crop residue**, or **dung cakes** as primary or secondary energy sources due to cost factors.

questions.question: In tennis a player/team needs to win ____ consecutive points after deuce to win a game.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The standard scoring system in **tennis** progresses through a sequence of **0 (Love)**, **15**, **30**, and **40** points. A player wins a game after scoring four points, provided they have a lead of at least two points.
 
• A **Deuce** occurs when both players or teams reach a score of **40-40**. This indicates a tie at the threshold of winning, triggering a requirement for a **two-point advantage** to conclude the game.
 
• To win the game from a deuce, a player or team must win **2 consecutive points**. The first point won after a deuce is known as the **Advantage** point.
 
• If the player holding the advantage wins the following point, they win the game. However, if they lose that point, the score reverts to **Deuce**, and the cycle continues until one side achieves the necessary **2** back-to-back points.
 
• This mechanism ensures that the winner of a game demonstrates a clear margin of superiority at the final stage of the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advantage Nomenclature**:

 
 
• **Advantage In (Ad-In)**: Used when the **server** wins the point following a deuce.
 
• **Advantage Out (Ad-Out)**: Used when the **receiver** wins the point following a deuce.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background**:
 
 
• The term **Deuce** is thought to originate from the French phrase **'à deux de jeu'**, which means **'two points away from the game'**.
 
• The **International Tennis Federation (ITF)** sets the rules for professional matches, ensuring consistency across global tournaments like the **Grand Slams**.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Scoring**:
 
 
• Some formats, particularly in doubles or junior matches, use **No-Ad scoring** (No-Advantage). In this system, a single **deciding point** is played at deuce, and the winner of that point immediately wins the game.
 
 
 
• **Set and Match Rules**:
 
 
• Just as games require a two-point margin from deuce, a **set** typically requires a **two-game lead** (e.g., 6-4). If a set reaches **6-6**, a **Tie-break** is usually played where the first to **7 points** with a two-point margin wins.
 
 

Therefore, the correct option is 2
